{{other people|Alexander Grossmann}}
{{Use American English|date=September 2026}}
'''Alexander Grossmann''' (5 August 1930 – 12 February 2019) was a [[France|French]]-[[America]]n [[physicist]] of [[Croatia]]n origin.

==Early life==
Aleksandar Grossmann was born to a Jewish family in [[Zagreb]], where he was attending a [[gymnasium (school)|gymnasium]] when [[World War II in Yugoslavia]] started. Forced to flee the so-called [[Independent State of Croatia]] in April 1941, he and his family settled in [[Rijeka]] in Italy-occupied Croatia, then in [[Montecatini Terme]] in Italy, and finally [[Switzerland]]. After the war, he returned to Zagreb and completed high school as well as graduated mathematics at the [[Faculty of Science, University of Zagreb]] in 1952.<ref name="ZBL">{{cite encyclopedia | url = https://zbl.lzmk.hr/?p=132 | language = hr | title = GROSSMANN, Aleksandar (Alexander, Alex) | encyclopedia = Jewish Biographical Lexicon | publisher = [[Miroslav Krleža Institute of Lexicography]] | access-date = 2024-09-23 }}</ref>

==Career==
Grossmann started work at the [[Ruđer Bošković Institute]], and collaborated with international visiting scholars between 1952 and 1955.<ref name="ZBL"/>

He travelled to the United States in 1955, working in the physics departments of the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] (IAS) in Princeton, [[Brandeis University]], and the [[Courant Institute]], [[NYU]], then again at the IAS <ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ias.edu/scholars/alexander-grossmann|title=Alexander Grossmann|date=9 December 2019|access-date=2021-04-15}}</ref> until 1963.

After one year at the [[Institut des Hautes Études Scientifiques]] (IHES) in Bures-sur-Yvette, France, he joined the "Centre de Physique Théorique de Marseille" (the CPT) as it was being created in 1966, at the request of [[Daniel Kastler]]. He then became a research supervisor at the [[CNRS]].<ref>{{cite web|title=A celebration for Alexandre Grossmann and Yves Meyer - Sciencesconf.org|url=https://grossmann-meyer.sciencesconf.org/|website=grossmann-meyer.sciencesconf.org/resource/page/id/4|access-date=2021-03-22}}</ref>

At the [[Université de la Méditerranée Aix-Marseille II]] in [[Luminy]] campus he did pioneering work on [[wavelet]] analysis with [[Jean Morlet]] in 1984.<ref>{{Cite journal |doi=10.1137/0515056 |title=Decomposition of Hardy Functions into Square Integrable Wavelets of Constant Shape |journal = SIAM Journal on Mathematical Analysis|volume = 15|issue = 4|pages = 723–736|year = 1984|last1 = Grossmann|first1 = A.|last2 = Morlet|first2 = J.}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |author=Norbert Verdier|date=2009-04-27 |title=H37 & QDL 26: Jean Morlet et ses ondelettes|publisher=Accueil |url=http://www.les-mathematiques.net/ |access-date=2025-07-09 |website=Les-mathematiques.net |language=fr}}</ref> This in effect showed this identity's applicability to signal analysis.<ref>{{Cite book | title =  Wavelets| url =  https://archive.org/details/waveletstoolsfor00jaff_431| url-access =  limited|pages = [https://archive.org/details/waveletstoolsfor00jaff_431/page/n29 15]–33|doi = 10.1137/1.9780898718119.ch2|chapter = 2. Wavelets from a Historical Perspective|year = 2001|isbn = 978-0-89871-448-7|last1 = Jaffard|first1 = Stephane|last2 = Meyer|first2 = Yves|last3 = Ryan|first3 = Robert D.}}</ref>

In 1993, he became involved in genomic research as part of a group formed in [[Gif-sur-Yvette]]. He worked in this area with what eventually became the Laboratoire de Mathématique & Modélisation d'Evry until 2014.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.cpt.univ-mrs.fr/spip.php?page=article&id_article=169|title=Alexandre J. Grossmann (1930 - 2019) - Centre de Physique Théorique}}</ref>

==Tributes==
Grossmann's lifelong scientific achievements were commemorated at a scientific conference held in his honor and that of [[Yves Meyer]] on 12-13 June 2019 at the Institut de Mathématiques d'Orsay.<ref>{{cite web|title=A celebration for Alexandre Grossmann and Yves Meyer - Sciencesconf.org|url=https://grossmann-meyer.sciencesconf.org/|website=grossmann-meyer.sciencesconf.org|access-date=2019-08-05}}</ref>
